overall.note: M1–M6/M8 demonstrate a productive connected application core with no established backend defect. Typed transactions, subscriptions and scheduling fit directly; durable offline storage and specialized media delivery remained substantial application responsibilities.

writes_and_transactions.note: M2/M3/M8 diary: atomic mutations combined DM deduplication, recipient capture, intent ledgers, counters and scheduling. Full replay independently verified all 167,157 actions; no transaction defect was recorded.

offline_sync.note: M5/M6 diary and essay: no integrated durable queue or native local database; account caches, ordered outbox, media persistence and expiry enforcement were authored separately. Web convergence passed; unfinished native proofs do not establish a backend defect.

media_assets.note: M4/M5 diary: ordinary storage upload/delete was compact; recipient-specific view-once delivery required a consuming claim/action and transient bytes. Durable media storage and revocation-aware client caches remained application work.

background_work.note: M3/M8 diary: scheduling supported typing cleanup, expiry and per-user digest jobs without a separate worker service. Real scheduled emission passed; final-report restart-deduplication verification remained incomplete, without an observed scheduler defect.

client_integration.note: M1–M3/M8 diary: React query subscriptions made connected multi-device behavior direct. M6 required session-aware persistence and native lifecycle glue; the React Native window crash is explicitly agent-error.

diagnostics_dev_loop.note: M1/M8 logs describe generated types, watcher deployment and explicit BadAdminKey/function-not-found refusals supporting correction. Final-report attributes all 29 correction episodes to agent/environment causes, with no demonstrated Convex defect.

scale_and_limits.note: Final-report: full replay, deep paging, 500-follow and celebrity read/write probes passed. Trending's strict midpoint check failed. Cold-sync memory and busy-group visual behavior were unmeasured; no backend capability ceiling was established.

convex.verdict: Convex provided the most straightforward connected application workflow, with durable offline behavior its largest missing subsystem.

overall.note: M1–M6/M8 web and eventual native proofs demonstrate feasibility. SQL, managed auth and Storage fit well, while synchronization, authorization composition and worker infrastructure remained application-owned. No Supabase defect was established.

setup_and_docs.note: M1 diary/essay: documented managed auth, Storage and hosted SQL were straightforward. Immediate signup used admin createUser followed by password sign-in; shared-project namespacing and the unavailable local CLI were deployment-context requirements.

authorization.note: M1/M3–M5 diary: membership predicates and atomic view ledgers worked; immediate logout required a deny list, and private assets needed an authenticated authorization route. Evidence covers API-owned policies across several entry points.

queries_and_live.note: M2/M5 diary: relational feeds and indexed prefix search were expressive; live projections used authored polling and offline search duplication. Realtime was unexercised. M4 polling starvation was agent-error and receives no backend-defect penalty.

writes_and_transactions.note: M2/M3/M6 diary: SQL transactions, unique pairs and an intent ledger handled recipient capture and retry safety. Final-report audits all 167,157 ordered settlements; replay uses the canonical app mutation with disclosed staged transport.

offline_sync.note: M6 diary/native follow-ups: ordered outbox, per-user history, media files, search and revocation policy were authored separately. Both native proofs eventually passed; the exercised SDK supplied no integrated offline queue or local query store.

media_assets.note: M4/M5 diary: Storage upload/download was straightforward. Membership revocation and expiry required an authenticated proxy; view-once required atomic consumption records and transient client bytes. Ordinary offline media persistence was application-owned.

background_work.note: M8 diary/essay: SQL aggregates and unique period/emission records supported a closed-client digest restart and authorization proof. Scheduling, connection tracking and push emission used an application-owned Node worker/provider seam.

client_integration.note: M1–M6 diary: managed auth/Storage integrated with Expo, but API transport, polling, token refresh, reconnect and persistent caches needed explicit wiring. Final-report confirms native proofs passed after application fixes; Realtime was not exercised.

diagnostics_dev_loop.note: Scale run-log: EXPLAIN, relational audits, explicit expired-principal refusal and accurate rate-limit documentation supported diagnosis. The pool crash resulted from an omitted error handler, not a demonstrated Supabase defect.

scale_and_limits.note: Final-report: 167,157 actions and 1,002 chats verified after recovery; 7/9 read comparisons passed. Documented Auth limits required pacing. Midpoint misses remain ambiguous; staged replay and absent celebrity-write/cold-sync proofs qualify confidence.

operations.note: M6/M8 and scale report: SQL migrations, durable settlement receipts and exact catalog/identity audits enabled recovery and verified cleanup. Hosted Auth, buckets, schemas and the local API required separate lifecycle management.

supabase.verdict: Supabase was a strong relational foundation whose managed services saved work, while this architecture retained extensive synchronization and process responsibilities.
supabase.would_use_again_for: I would use it again for relational social products with reporting and custom server workflows where owning the synchronization layer is acceptable.

cross_backend_notes: All three report M1–M6 and M8 web green; Supabase subsequently obtained both native proofs, while the other lanes' incomplete native qualification does not establish backend incapability.

Snapback's integrated carrier, asset authority and resumable jobs removed infrastructure, but its explicitly attributed conditional-envelope defect and canonical-history certification refusal warrant backend deductions.

Convex's transaction/subscription workflow minimized connected-client coordination; Supabase's relational querying was especially direct, while its chosen polling/API/worker design provides no evidence that Supabase Realtime or alternative scheduling surfaces were unavailable.

Convex and Supabase receive equal offline penalties for supplying no integrated durable queue/query store through the exercised surface, with Supabase's native success establishing feasibility through additional application work.

Overall scores are holistic rather than category averages, and scale judgments use verified coverage and documented constraints rather than local-versus-hosted timings, correction counts or agent/environment/ambiguous failures; M7 was untested throughout.
